SMTO-SKL-0177 — GitHub couldn't find this release

GUID: 46cf2706-633f-52cc-94b4-cfc4a546d6e9
Slug: github-release-not-found
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: github

What happened

  • SMTO asked GitHub for a release (a published version of the project) or its version tag, and GitHub couldn't find it. The name may be wrong, or your GitHub account in SMTO can't see it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On github.com, open the GitHub project and select Releases (and Tags) to find the exact release or version tag you meant. A wrong release or tag name is the most common reason GitHub reports it missing.
  2. If you are creating a new release, make sure its version tag already exists on GitHub. If not, ask the Agent to create and push the tag from your project folder first. SMTO only makes releases for tags that already exist; it never creates the tag for you.
  3. Ask the Agent again, naming the exact release or tag. If it's still not found, ask whoever set up your GitHub Account in Parameter Store to check it covers this project. GitHub reports releases your access key can't see as not found.

What success looks like

  • The Agent shows the release's details, or the new draft release appears under Releases on github.com.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages your GitHub access in SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A GitHub release operation (release_*) received a 404 for the release, its assets, or the tag that release_create requires to already exist; GitHub also returns 404 when the token cannot see the resource.

What this means

  • A release-prefixed operation receives HTTP 404 for a release or related resource. This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.

Why this can happen

  • A release-prefixed operation receives HTTP 404 for a release or related resource.

How to diagnose it

  • Verify exact release/tag/asset route and Contents permission.

How to fix it

  • Read the exact release ID with github.releases in the same repository, or for release_create confirm the tag already exists (SMTO never creates tags; push it with Git first). A 404 can also mean the token lacks contents:read/contents:write or is not scoped to this repository; correct the token, then update granted_permissions in the GitHub Account profile in Parameter Store.
  • Read the exact release ID or existing tag in this repository with Contents access; 404 can mean inaccessible.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended existing release resource is resolved in the same repository.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
